response.content:
## Cloud and Data Centre Companies That Entered the Finnish Market in 2026

Finland has seen a remarkable wave of new cloud and data centre entrants in 2026, driven by the country's cold climate, cheap renewable energy, and growing AI infrastructure demand. Here are the key companies that entered or announced their entry into the Finnish market this year:

### New Entrants / First Major Finnish Projects in 2026

1. **Nebius Group** (Amsterdam-based AI infrastructure firm) — In March 2026, Nebius announced a 310 MW data centre in Lappeenranta, near Finland's eastern border, with an estimated value exceeding $10 billion. It also tripled capacity at its existing Mäntsälä site to 75 MW (up to 60,000 GPUs). This represents one of Finland's largest infrastructure projects to date.

2. **Sesterce** (French AI infrastructure group) — In October 2026, Sesterce announced plans for a €10 billion+ AI data centre campus in Jämsä, on the site of a former paper mill. The first phase (200 MW) has works planned to start in 2026, scaling to 600 MW and eventually over 1 GW.

3. **Cerebras Systems** (US AI chip company) — Announced a new 165 MW AI data centre in Mikkeli, Finland, in partnership with Compute Nordic Finland. Construction on the initial 50 MW phase is already under way. Cerebras also signed contracts for additional capacity in Finland during Q3 2026.

4. **GleSYS** (Swedish cloud and infrastructure provider) — In June 2026, GleSYS signed an agreement with Trevian Asset Management to establish Campus Oulu, an AI-ready data centre campus with expansion potential up to 300 MW. The first 8 MW phase was targeted for service in autumn 2026. GleSYS had acquired a Finnish data centre business in 2024 but significantly expanded its footprint in 2026.

5. **Hyperco / Edgnex** (Damac-backed, acquired by Edgnex in April 2025) — Filed permit applications in 2026 for a new 100 MW data centre in Kouvola (to serve TikTok/ByteDance) and is developing additional sites in Espoo, Pyhäjoki, and Lohja.

6. **QTS** (US-based data centre REIT) — Received zoning approval for a campus outside Forssa, Finland, on a 150-hectare site that could total 700,000 sqm.

7. **DayOne** — An international operator looking to develop in Finland, listed among newer entrants planning facilities in the country.

8. **Scale42** — A newer operator planning multiple data centre developments in Finland.

9. **Polarnode** — A Finnish developer building the Nebius data centre in Lappeenranta and involved in other projects.

10. **FCDC Corp** — Among the leading upcoming market players with significant planned capacity in Finland.

### Expanding Existing Presence (Major 2026 Announcements)

- **Google** — Announced in September 2026 its largest-ever European investment: at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in AI infrastructure across Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala, to be deployed in 2027–2028. Google already operated in Finland but massively scaled its commitment.
- **Microsoft** and **TikTok** are also listed among major operators/investors developing large campuses and hyperscale facilities in Finland.
- **atNorth** (Icelandic data centre company) — Announced a new data centre in Salo, Finland, expanding its Nordic footprint.
- **Applied Digital** — Secured up to 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland.

### Market Context

Finland's data centre market is projected to grow from roughly $952 million in 2025 to $5.8 billion by 2031 (CAGR of ~35%). The country now has 24–25 existing facilities and 60+ planned or under-construction projects, with total upcoming capacity exceeding 5 GW. Over $30 billion in combined investments from Google, Microsoft, TikTok, and others have been committed or announced for Finland.

# Data center development planned for 180-hectare plot in Isojoki, Finland. Few details available, but local government has agreed land sale. Another large-scale data center development could be coming to Finland. Local press, including Yle, reports the Isojoki municipal government is selling a plot of approximately 180 hectares near the Pettenkangas industrial area for €10 million ($11.6m) for a planned data center project. A firm known as Isojoki Data Center Oy, reportedly backed by a Nordic real estate development company, is leading the project. Few details are available, but construction could start as soon as September 2026. Isojoki is a municipality of Finland. It is part of the South Ostrobothnia region on the western side of the country. The Pettenkangas industrial area is set to be home to a bioterminal that supports energy wood harvesting and wood chip entrepreneurship. Most of Finland’s data centers are located in the country’s capital, Helsinki. Established operators, including the likes of Verne, Equinix, and atNorth, have a presence in Finland, while newer operators such as Scale42, Polarnode, FCDC, Arcem, and Hyperco are planning multiple developments totaling gigawatts of capacity across the country. International operators, including QTS and DayOne, are also looking to develop in Finland. Earlier this month, the Forssa City Council approved the Ratasmäki and Rytökallio zoning plans that would allow QTS to develop a campus outside Forssa. The 150-hectare site could total 700,000 sqm (7.53 million sq ft). Hyperco, which is developing a data center campus in Kouvola set to serve TikTok owner ByteDance, has submitted an environmental impact assessment program to the South-Eastern Finland Centre for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment (ELY) for the project. Set to be developed in Hiivuri, the campus will total 100MW initially.

context.content: # Meet the data center capital of Europe as Google joins Microsoft and TikTok in betting over $30.2 billion on Finland. Data center expansion in the world is changing fast: while the U.S. boasts "data center alley" in Virginia and tax incentives for data center investment, Finland has rapidly come onto the scene as one of the largest data center magnets in Europe. But the latest and largest commitment came Wednesday, when Google announced its largest investment in Europe yet: an investment of at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in AI infrastructure in Finland over the next two years. "This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," Google said in a statement. The data center project isn't the only investment Google is making into the country: it also signed an agreement with Finnish utility company Fortum to extend the life of a nuclear power plant in Loviisa in the company's latest attempt to use nuclear power as a clean energy source to power the data center investment.
